recent_articles.title: Bihar CM woos investors with amended package, says govt.’s top priority is ensuring safety - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Samrat Choudhary**, the Chief Minister of Bihar, emphasized the government's commitment to ensuring the security of businessmen and boosting industrial growth in the state. He inaugurated a business conclave organized by the **Bihar Chamber of Commerce and Industries** to mark its centenary year. The CM highlighted the "Bihar Industrial Investment Promotion Package-2025" aimed at attracting private investment, while assuring investors that their safety is paramount. Choudhary also addressed concerns about crime and caste politics, stating that criminals are not defined by their background and the government will prioritize investor security.

recent_articles.title: Setback for NDA as RJD wins MLC byelection in Bihar - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD)** won the Bhojpur-Buxar Legislative Council seat in a byelection, defeating the **National Democratic Alliance (NDA)** candidate. **Sonu Rai**, representing the RJD, secured victory with 2,486 votes, while his opponent, **Kanhaiya Prasad** of the JD(U), received 2,146 votes. The RJD has attributed their win to alleged manipulation and fraud in the electoral process.

recent_articles.title: Nitish and BJP have no moral right to speak on dynastic politics, says Tejashwi Yadav - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Tejashwi Yadav**, leader of the opposition in Bihar's Legislative Assembly, criticized **Nitish Kumar** and **Prime Minister Narendra Modi** for their involvement in dynasty politics following the expansion of the **Bihar Cabinet**.  Yadav argued that both the **BJP** and its allies are engaging in dynasty politics, citing examples like the inclusion of sons of former Chief Ministers in the new cabinet.

recent_articles.title: Kerala Assembly Elections 2026: IUML enters new era as Fathima Thahiliya becomes first woman MLA - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Fathima Thahiliya**, a former Haritha leader and practicing lawyer, has become the first woman from the **Indian Union Muslim League (IUML)** to be elected to the Kerala Assembly.  She defeated **T.P. Ramakrishnan**, the LDF convener, by a significant margin of 5,087 votes. This victory marks a turning point for the IUML, which had previously faced criticism for its lack of female representation in public life. The party's leadership has increasingly embraced women's participation in politics, as evidenced by their decision to field two women candidates this election.  While Ms. Thahiliya's win is a significant step forward, it also signals the potential for broader acceptance of women within the IUML's electoral framework.

recent_articles.title: BJP attacking Bengali culture, pride: Kejriwal; Modi won’t have his way in Bengal: Tejashwi - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Arvind Kejriwal**, former Delhi Chief Minister and convener of the **Aam Aadmi Party**, joined the Trinamool Congress campaign in West Bengal on Sunday, addressing three rallies in Kolkata and Howrah.  His visit coincides with the final days of campaigning for the second phase of the Assembly elections, scheduled to conclude Monday evening. The AAP recently experienced a setback as seven of its MPs switched to the **Bharatiya Janata Party**.

recent_articles.title: Election Commission, and not the BJP, seems to be fighting Trinamool in West Bengal, says Kapil Sibal - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Kapil Sibal**, a senior Supreme Court lawyer and Rajya Sabha MP, criticized the **Election Commission of India (ECI)**'s actions in West Bengal ahead of the upcoming elections. He accused the **EC** and the **BJP** of working together to suppress the Trinamool Congress (TMC), alleging an "unconstitutional Emergency" and a disproportionate deployment of Central Armed Police Forces (CAPF).  Other opposition leaders, including **Arvind Kejriwal**, have also expressed concern over the situation.

recent_articles.title: Poll bugle to fall silent across Tamil Nadu on Tuesday evening - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Political parties** in Tamil Nadu are concluding their intense campaigning ahead of the Assembly election on April 23rd.  Polling will begin at 7 a.m. that day, with all political functionaries and party workers not eligible to vote required to vacate the area by 6 p.m. on Tuesday. **Prime Minister Narendra Modi**, **Rahul Gandhi**, and other prominent leaders from various parties have campaigned in the state, while the Chief Electoral Officer has outlined strict regulations for the period leading up to the election.  These include restrictions on public gatherings, vehicle usage, and the establishment of polling booths.

recent_articles.title: ​A plan of change: On Bihar politics and the BJP - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Samrat Choudhary**, a former member of the Rashtriya Janata Dal and Janata Dal (United), was sworn in as the 24th Chief Minister of Bihar on April 15, 2026.  This marks the first time a politician from the **Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)** has held the office. The BJP's strategy for growth involved outgrowing regional partners and shifting power dynamics within the state, culminating in Choudhary's appointment after years of maneuvering.  The move signifies a shift in Bihar's political landscape as the BJP seeks to solidify its hold on the OBC-EBC base that was previously held by **Nitish Kumar**.

recent_articles.title: Bihar CM slams opposition over women's quota bill - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary** criticized the opposition parties for their refusal to support an amendment to the women's reservation bill, calling it a "black day" and vowing retaliation. **Sanjay Saraogi**, state party president of the BJP, announced that the party's women's wing would hold a protest on April 20th against the opposition's stance. The amendment, which grants 33% reservation to women in Parliament, was passed by an overwhelming majority in 2023 but faced opposition from non-NDA parties who were wary of its link with delimitation.

recent_articles.title: It’ a red-letter day, says Revanth; KTR blames BJP - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: Following the defeat of the Women's Reservation Bill in Parliament, **Congress** and **Bharatiya Rashtra Samithi (BRS)** leaders praised opposition parties for uniting to block the controversial legislation.  **Rahul Gandhi**, **Mallikarjun Kharge**, and **A. Revanth Reddy** led the charge against the bill, with **K. T. Rama Rao** blaming the BJP for its failure. **Bandi Sanjay** accused the Congress of using the bill to weaken southern India, while **N Ramchander Rao** criticized the bill's defeat as a setback for women's empowerment.

recent_articles.title: Beneath the euphoria, Bihar’s first BJP Chief Minister faces several significant challenges - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: Newly sworn-in **Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary**, a former Deputy Chief Minister in the previous Nitish Kumar government, faces significant challenges as he assumes leadership of Bihar.  **Choudhary**, who joined the BJP in 2017 after a career in opposition parties, must navigate complex coalition dynamics and match the political persona of his predecessor while managing high expectations from the people. He also needs to address financial mismanagement, communal harmony concerns, and doubts about his abilities within the BJP and its ideological parent organization, the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS).  **Choudhary** will need to establish his administrative capabilities in a state known for groupism among bureaucrats and broaden the BJP's voter base while maintaining alliances with existing parties.

recent_articles.title: Samrat Choudhary sworn in as Bihar’s first BJP CM - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Samrat Choudhary**, newly elected leader of the **National Democratic Alliance (NDA)**, was sworn in as the Chief Minister of Bihar on Wednesday.  He was accompanied by two senior JD(U) leaders, **Bijendra Prasad Yadav** and **Vijay Kumar Choudhary**, who are expected to serve as Deputy CMs. The swearing-in ceremony took place at Lok Bhawan with prominent figures from the BJP and former CM Nitish Kumar in attendance.  The new government is expected to expand after the results of upcoming state elections.

recent_articles.title: INDIA bloc opposes Delimitation Bill - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Mallikarjun Kharge**, president of the **All India Congress Committee (AICC)**, announced that the INDIA bloc has unanimously decided to oppose the Delimitation Bill.  **Kharge** stated that opposition parties are not against the Women’s Reservation Bill but are concerned about the bill's linking with delimitation and seat increases in State Assemblies. Several Opposition leaders, including **T.R. Baalu**, **Tejashwi Yadav**, and **Sanjay Raut**, expressed their opposition to the Delimitation Bill.

recent_articles.title: Noida workers’ protests: Two RJD spokespersons booked for sharing ‘misleading’ video, inciting tension - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD)** spokespersons **Priyanka Bharti** and **Kanchana Yadav** have been accused of sharing a video from Madhya Pradesh on social media, falsely linking it to the ongoing labor protests in Noida.  They are also being investigated for inciting tension by posting about the incident on X and Facebook. The **Uttar Pardesh Police** have registered an FIR against them and the X handle @ItsKtyni, alleging they spread rumors during the protests.

recent_articles.title: Bihar political history timeline: 1990 to 2026 - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Nitish Kumar**, the long-serving Chief Minister of Bihar, is set to resign on April 14, 2026, after a two-decade tenure.  Kumar's resignation follows his successful re-election as Chief Minister in 2025 and his nomination for the Rajya Sabha. The BJP will appoint its first Chief Minister in the state, marking a significant shift in Bihar's political landscape. Kumar's departure opens the door for a new chapter in Bihar's governance.
